plan: With 3 bidders and values uniform on [0,49], the optimal first-price auction strategy is to bid a fraction (n-1)/n of my value, since competitors follow similar logic and this maximizes expected profit while maintaining a good win probability. With n=3, I should bid approximately 2/3 of my value: 49 × (2/3) ≈ 32.7. This balances winning probability against paying too much, assuming rational competitors bid similarly based on their own values.

With 3 bidders and values uniform on $0-$49, the Nash equilibrium bidding strategy in a first-price auction is to bid (n-1)/n times your value, which here is 2/3. This balances winning probability against profit margin. My value is $44, so I'll bid approximately $29.30 to shade appropriately below my value while remaining competitive against the other two bidders' likely bids.

With 3 bidders and uniform values on [0,49], the optimal first-price auction strategy is to bid a fraction of my value to balance winning probability against profit margin. The theoretical optimal bid shading factor is (n-1)/n = 2/3 for risk-neutral bidders in this symmetric setting. My value is $22, so I'll bid approximately 2/3 of that to maximize expected profit while still maintaining a reasonable chance of winning.
